extracted.intended_audience: general newspaper readers (wartime Associated Press audience); newspaper editors/reporters
extracted.subtask_description: Reporting and presenting breaking wartime news for a general newspaper audience (Associated Press-style wire copy) including datelines, official communiqués, casualty lists, political coverage and labor/administrative developments. Emphasizes attribution, specific details, chronology and context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dateline and wire attribution
rubrics_metrics.description: Include location and date at the top of items and attribute to the wire service (e.g., 'Allied Headquarters in Australia, May 17 (A. P.).', 'WASHINGTON, May 17—(AP)').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dateline+service establishes when and where the report originated and that it is wire copy; use consistently at starts of discrete items. Examples on page: multiple items begin with 'WASHINGTON, May 17—(AP)' or 'Allied Headquarters in Australia, May 17 (A. P.).' to show provenance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attribute statements to named official sources
rubrics_metrics.description: When reporting claims or denials, identify the official source (e.g., 'a navy spokesman said', 'the navy denied', 'President Roosevelt ... the White House disclosed', 'Gen. Hershey testified').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer explicit attributions for contested facts or official positions; examples include the navy denying Tokyo radio claims and quotations attributed to the President, senators, or selective service director. Attribution signals where the information came from and whether it is an official position.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flag unconfirmed or enemy-broadcast items
rubrics_metrics.description: Clearly mark items that are unconfirmed or originate from enemy/foreign broadcasts (e.g., 'The Tokyo radio—unconfirm from any sources in Washington—also has reported...').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicate uncertainty and source so readers can judge reliability. The page marks Tokyo radio reports as unconfirmed and contrasts them with official U.S. denials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use official communiqués verbatim when available
rubrics_metrics.description: When a military or government communiqué exists, quote its wording directly (e.g., the navy communique: 'Operations against the Japanese on Attu Island are continuing.').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quoting communiqués preserves official phrasing and avoids paraphrase errors; the page quotes the navy communique and lists navy communique No. 379 results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide concrete numbers and specifics
rubrics_metrics.description: Give quantitative details (casualty totals, numbers of ships sunk, numbers of men in categories) rather than vague phrases (e.g., 'the navy has reported 23,955 casualties', 'Army casualties reported through May 7 total 56,942').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Precise figures enhance credibility and usefulness for readers; the page supplies detailed casualty breakdowns and counts of ships sunk/damaged by submarines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish fact, opinion and speculation
rubrics_metrics.description: Label assertions of policy or strategy that are opinions or proposals (e.g., 'Senator Chandler proposed change in strategy', 'he contended', 'one authority went so far as to say "one good day of clear weather is all we need."').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use verbs like 'said', 'asserted', 'contended', 'predicted' to signal opinion; contextualize such statements rather than presenting them as established fact. The page separates senators' arguments from confirmed operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide chronological context and sequence
rubrics_metrics.description: Situate events in time (e.g., 'The drive began last Tuesday', 'the navy late today broke a three-day silence').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timelines help readers understand progress and what preceded events. The page repeatedly notes when campaigns began and how long silence or delays lasted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explain consequences and operational context
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain strategic implications and possible follow-on actions (e.g., 'With control of Attu ... an attack upon Kiska could be launched from two sides', 'another offensive move possible after Attu is wholly in American hands is bombing of ... Paramushiru').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adding operational context helps readers grasp significance beyond immediate events; the article links local actions to broader strategy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use direct quotations to convey tone and exact messages
rubrics_metrics.description: Include verbatim quotations for important statements (e.g., Roosevelt's messages, senators' remarks, 'Enemy claims ... are absolutely untrue').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quotations capture tone and exact wording; the page reproduces key lines from Roosevelt's messages and official denials and senators' statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organize content with clear headings/subheads
rubrics_metrics.description: Use bolded or capitalized section headings to separate topics (e.g., 'KISKA ATTACK PLAN', 'HERSHEY SAYS DRAFT MAY DIP', 'Navy’s Losses First 17 Months, 23,955; Army’s, 56,942').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Headings help readers scan a complex page with multiple items (military operations, politics, labor disputes, casualty lists). The page demonstrates multiple topical subheads.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report denials and counterclaims explicitly
rubrics_metrics.description: When an opposing side makes a claim (especially wartime propaganda), publish official denials and the denying source (e.g., 'The navy denied ... "Enemy claims ... are absolutely untrue," a navy spokesman said').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publishing denials alongside claims provides balance and lets readers see contested narratives; the page shows Tokyo radio claims followed by navy denials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include human-identifying details in casualty/ casualty-list reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: When listing killed/wounded/missing, provide names, ranks and next-of-kin details (the page contains many entries listing names, ranks and relatives' addresses).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detailed identification helps families and communities recognize individuals and lends completeness to casualty reporting; the format on the page shows name, rank and relative/address for many men.
